# Orchestration (area `orchestration`)

Planner and workers, task lifecycle, questions, pause/stop, schedules, reminders, loops and continuity between turns.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **ORCH-300** (owner): FERB has no notification rules: no planner field, side entry, RPC, CLI command or policy hook for them.
- **ORCH-301** (owner): Delegated conversations (converse steps) and answering FERB's questions in chat stay.
- **ORCH-302** (owner): One checker role judges an attempt's conditions and chooses what comes next (accept, fix the answer, retry with instructions, ask the owner, accept as unconfirmed, fail). There is no separate dispatcher.
- **ORCH-303** (owner): The planner gets the running summary for everything older plus the last 20 exchanges word for word (20 owner messages and FERB's replies to them), never history filling the model's window. Long task reports appear in their short form. The last 20 exchanges are never shortened, folded or dropped, however long they are.
- **ORCH-304** (owner): The summary holds the recent ~2 weeks plus what is still open (waiting tasks, open questions, promises); older settled material falls out of it, since memory facts and episodes hold what lasts. It folds about every 20-40 exchanges, in the background after the reply; the planner reads only the latest summary.
- **ORCH-305** (owner): There is no separate map step: a do step may carry an input list, independent steps run in parallel, and plan validation keeps the check that every input is covered exactly once.
- **ORCH-306** (owner): Standing sends stay: they are the only way to send to recipients FERB found itself (not in the owner's words, not already known), and the only way an unattended run can do so. Recipients in the owner's words or approved once never ask anyway.
- **ORCH-307** (owner): Attempts are counted per task or plan step: worker runs in one attempt loop, not model calls, tool calls or time; each loop round starts at 0. After 5 failed attempts FERB pauses and asks whether to keep going: Yes allows 5 more, No stops with what it found. An unattended run can't ask, so it stops at 5 and reports.
- **ORCH-308** (owner): Pause ends the current attempt and marks the task paused, not cancelled: no task-end clean-up, no final answer, loop state kept. Resume continues in place with the owner's discussion as the update, on the shared wait-for-the-owner mechanism. The planner pauses a running task when the owner's words question, doubt or rethink it (its reading, no keyword list); a plain correction still steers live. No pause button in the app.
- **ORCH-309** (owner): A task is done when every outcome condition is verified; an unproven side detail is removed from the answer or marked inline (fix the answer, no redo), so FERB never states unseen things as fact. How the work was done is judged from code facts, not by the model. Done-unconfirmed only when an outcome itself can't be verified. Every answer: the answer first, then at most one short "Couldn't confirm: ..." line; no "Why work stopped" on finished work, no restated goal.
- **ORCH-312** (owner): Pausing stops the task's running terminal commands and audio listening and keeps only its tabs and progress. FERB mentions a paused task once a day ("<task> is still paused. Resume?"). Pausing a scheduled run pauses that schedule's next runs.
- **ORCH-313** (owner): Folders, recipients and sites, profile/account, worker type and standing scope are fixed when a schedule or reminder is made, and stated then so the owner can correct them; unattended runs never re-guess them.
- **ORCH-314** (owner): Failed scheduled runs add no check-in across runs: each failed run already reports in chat.
- **ORCH-315** (owner): When the configured runtime reports a usage limit or a sign-in failure, FERB says so once and offers another signed-in runtime with one tap. It never switches by itself (billing).
- **ORCH-317** (owner): Reminders and schedules can fire when the owner is back at the Mac instead of polling; a scheduled run that did nothing posts nothing. Back at the Mac means the Mac coming back into use: lid opened or wake from sleep, screen unlocked, login or restart. Input idleness is not away: watching a film without touching anything is still being at the Mac. The paused-task mention uses the same signal.
- **ORCH-319** (owner): A part is one of the owner's asks, not a plan step. The planner declares parts in the owner's order, each answered directly or by one answer step; code validates them (one answer source each, answer steps distinct and not wait/ask, each success condition in exactly one part, no summing-up step). Tool-free parts answer in the first reply. Each other part posts once, when its answer step's check accepts, recorded durably, never twice, also across restarts. No final summarizing call: code adds only its fixed lines and "N of M done".
- **ORCH-320** (owner): When the request gives an end ("until Nov 3", "for 2 weeks"), the schedule stores it (quote-checked like every side entry), stops after it, and its card counts down to it. No end date in the words: it runs until stopped.
- **ORCH-321** (owner): A payment card shows the name the owner saved the card under in FERB (recorded with the payment when a saved card entry filled it), never any card digits.
- **ORCH-322** (agent): Every tree runs as a plan of worker steps with dependencies; a single task is a one-step plan. Step kinds are do (optional input list; an optional repeat rule makes it a loop), wait, ask and converse. A loop is a do step with a repeat rule on the same path, ending on a verified condition or a stop.
- **ORCH-323** (agent): Tree, step, loop round and conversation turn share one status function, one finish function, one stop check and one injected clock. "Needs the owner" means one thing everywhere: pause in place and ask; an unattended run declines at once. task.finished is published once per tree.
- **ORCH-324** (agent): A typed per-turn object carries a chat turn; one exit applies side entries, records the reply and lets the chat go. One quote check (memory.items.quoted) serves every side entry (remember, until, timers, schedules, changes, cancels, forget, conversation changes). One continue verb corrects running and ended tasks.
- **ORCH-325** (agent): Planner context goes: instructions, stable facts, running summary, recent conversation (append-only), then the "Newly always on" entries (MEM-429), then the live facts, time, front window, task state and open questions, then the new message (2026-11-03: no pushed memory or activity, ORCH-515; the lookup tools' schemas are fixed per install, so they don't move the cached prefix). Live values stay out of the cached prefix: {capabilities} names the paired owner profiles only, and whether each is connected now is in "Layer 2 - right now".
- **ORCH-326** (agent): Beyond the last 20 exchanges the conversation folds into the summary once that tail holds FOLD_CHUNK_TOKENS (20k) or the whole tail passes RECENT_CONVERSATION_TOKENS + FOLD_CHUNK_TOKENS (35k), in calls of at most 20k each. The summary is asked to stay within SUMMARY_TOKENS (2k) and is cut to it when shown; SUMMARY_DAYS (14) is its ~2 weeks. A report's short form is its first paragraph, 300 chars; a multi-part task's index (ORCH-534) is shown whole, each of its lines clipped to 300.
- **ORCH-327** (agent): Task and schedule folders must each name one specific folder: the disk root, the home folder itself, /Volumes and iCloud Drive's root are sent back to the planner for repair (argument validity).
- **ORCH-329** (agent): Typed cards come only from rows FERB itself wrote: timer and schedule rows, memory items, a tool call's recorded kinds, target and page facts with the owner's Yes, the sites list, the artifacts, a schedule's run. No text is read to choose or fill a card. A card standing for one of code's lines names it, and the notch leaves that line out.
- **ORCH-330** (agent): New planner schema fields add no union or nullable types: unused fields are "" or 0, and flags are plain booleans.
- **ORCH-331** (agent): A one-step scheduled run (not a watch) that found nothing its request asks to tell and did nothing posts nothing (nothing_to_tell). The worker's word alone never silences a run: one whose tree has an acting call that ran without an error (cards.ACTING_KINDS) posts whatever its worker reported. Multi-step scheduled plans and planner replies always post.
- **ORCH-332** (agent): A chat.part record's seq is the UTC time to the microsecond as an ISO string, strictly increasing also across a restart.
- **ORCH-333** (owner): There is no separate resource reviewer: code records what the task closed or left open, and the merged checker judges it with everything else.
- **ORCH-334** (owner): A schedule's repeat interval is the owner's: code requires only a positive number, and no prompt sets a floor.
- **ORCH-500** (agent): intro.preview runs the real planner turn alone (Supervisor.preview): no run token, no worker, no task row, no chat entry; every event (plan, one part per planned step, done) carries preview: true. Its context leaves out the owner's live state (running tasks, open questions, earlier chat, notices, schedules, reminders) and keeps the capability facts; with no run token it has no lookups (ORCH-516), so no memory or activity. Its session prefix `preview:` is reserved, so chat.send refuses it. FERB.app only.
- **ORCH-503** (owner): For a big job the plan line states the plan, estimates and any standing scope, and work starts at once; the owner corrects by replying. Escape-hatch commands and retries after an unknown outcome still wait; steering never records a No; a retry the owner drives re-asks a No once.
- **ORCH-504** (owner): The daemon sends an instant acknowledgement from the owner's approved phrase list (ferb/orchestrator/acks.py, without the starred phrase), never one of the last eight used.
- **ORCH-505** (owner): A loop with no stated end runs until the owner says stop, across restarts and updates; when fixes don't last it backs off and tells the owner once; constants: backup round 1,800 s; didn't last within 120 s; 3 such in 600 s start back-off at 120 s doubling to 3,600 s; reset after 1,800 s; look-only rounds skip the check; held tabs return between rounds.
- **ORCH-506** (owner): Long-running watches run without AI calls (reload, read and view-switch clicks set up once), with a 30 s floor; FERB looks up the service's rate limits and says which interval it chose.
- **ORCH-507** (owner): A question stays open as long as its task waits, with no expiry. Codex's FERB tool timeout is MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT_S (7 days) and Claude Code's MCP tool idle timeout is off (CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT=0), so a waiting tool call isn't cut by the runtime.
- **ORCH-508** (agent): A stop from another chat stops a running task; a stop that arrives after the work finished leaves that work done, never cancelled; an answer to a question no longer waiting keeps the planner's own reply.
- **ORCH-509** (agent): An attempt whose report fails validation reports nothing of an earlier attempt, and a correction delivered while the check runs keeps the finished report for the next attempt, which starts from the correction.
- **ORCH-510** (agent): A clean shutdown runs no task-end clean-up for a task tree that resumes at the next start, so the change records startup keeps for it survive.
- **ORCH-511** (agent): An every-schedule resumed before its first run keeps that first run; a schedule whose timer was handled but not rebooked is rebooked once at start; a scheduled run never overlaps its previous run.
- **ORCH-512** (agent): A scheduled run keeps the recipients the owner said (a remembered address never rewrites them), and what an earlier run read from outside keeps its outside origin when the next run is shown that answer.
- **ORCH-514** (owner): The planner's Layer 1 device facts hold the macOS version, paired owner profiles, browser/profile inventory and worker types, but not the list of installed apps; running apps stay in the live facts. A task's worker looks apps up with its Mac tools (mac.apps) when a request involves one.
- **ORCH-515** (owner): Every planner turn gets its instructions with Tier 1, the summary and last 20 exchanges (ORCH-303), tasks running or waiting on the owner, open questions and live facts. Memory, older or other chats, this chat's other ended tasks and today's activity are not pushed: the planner looks them up, read-only, through FERB's gateway (ORCH-516). Kept from ORCH-1: the planner changes nothing until it returns; an observation or action on the Mac is a task. Kept from MEM-16: messages and FERB's short replies are in the fused search; chat.history searches by meaning and date, paging from the database.
- **ORCH-516** (agent): A planner call (not the intro preview: no run token) gets a run token for only PLANNER_TOOLS (memory.read, chat.history, task.evidence, trail.query, trail.days), observe-only, at most PLANNER_LOOKUPS (10) calls, for a live lookup record with no task row lent the turn's chat; all end with the call. Results reach the model as worker results do (redacted, with their origin line); their origins join the turn's and each becomes a planner read on its task, which the sink rule counts. No skill or ability catalog; a tool call restarts the reply draft.
- **ORCH-517** (agent): task.evidence takes an optional task_id: a task of the caller's conversation (the conversation of the caller's registered record, never a name), read whole (its tree's tool calls, records and reports) with that task's own origins; any other id is refused. Without it the tool reads the caller's own task as before.
- **ORCH-518** (owner): All of the owner's own chat message is their words (typed, pasted, > quoted, in a code block), with their authority exactly as typed text: every quote check, answers and corrections, and what the gateway counts as named by the owner. Kept from APP-584: no paste dialog; the composer still marks pastes for its local commands (APP-596). Still data: attached files and everything FERB reads (pages, mail, messages, screen, documents, clipboard reads, tool results). Pasted secrets are still masked (GATE-501).
- **ORCH-519** (owner): Every refusal by one of code's checks on a chat turn's side entries (the quote checks of reminders, schedules, end dates, schedule changes, reminder cancels, memory captures, forgets and conversation changes) tells the owner plainly that a safety check stopped it, which check, why in this case and what to do, in plain words with no ids (I12). One shared helper writes the line for every route (ferb/policy/blocked.py).
- **ORCH-520** (owner): (1) A quote may come from the owner's current message or their own earlier messages in the same chat; one source of the owner's words serves every quote check (reminders, schedules and their end dates, parts, memory, forget, changes, cancels, conversation changes). (2) FERB's reply reflects what actually happened: it never claims an action that code then refuses. (3) Bracketed-paste markers that leaked into the owner's message as text ("[200~ … [201~", with or without the ESC byte) are removed where chat text arrives: clean-up only, no reading of meaning.
- **ORCH-521** (agent): A correction records only destinations in the owner's words (pasted ones included, ORCH-518), keeps attachments as untrusted data, never widens a task's identity or scopes, redacts secrets before the worker and storage, and never answers a question or approves a payment, secret or plan unless the owner's own words name it.
- **ORCH-522** (agent): Every quote check reads Supervisor._said_in_chat: this turn's words, then this chat's earlier owner messages, newest first, only the last RECENT_EXCHANGES (20). Before a reply stands, each side entry the quote check would refuse is told back to the planner once through the repair path, so it rewrites its reply knowing it; one still refused after that never fails the turn: it is refused when applied and code's safety-check line follows the planner's text (ORCH-519).
- **ORCH-523** (agent): untrusted.mark records the owner's chat message whole as their words: the composer's bracketed-paste markers and leaked ones are removed, and > quote lines and ``` blocks are no longer split out as data. The [policy] pasted_text_is_data switch and the chat.message field pasted_as_owner_words are retired (the planner-cache check no longer reads them, RUN-416). Readers of older records still leave out the parts those records wrapped (typed_lines_of, recorded_own_words, WRAPPED); FERB's earlier question and attachment paths stay wrapped as data.
- **ORCH-524** (agent): A planner call carrying the owner's screenshot is run once more without it only on ImageRefused: the adapter marked the error as the provider's own image rejection (RUN-418). Any other failure (account, schema, timeout, network, no model) goes on as itself with its own words through the normal failure path (chat.failed), with no second call. `screen.image_refused` records the provider's words, not only an exception class.
- **ORCH-525** (agent): A chat turn's `planner.prepare` span (no task id, its request id) runs from its intake, after the chat.message rows, to its model.turn span, with steps_ms: messages, environment, front_window (the wait for the capture at send, DMN-520), runtime, conversation, live_facts, tasks, blocks; a repair or rerun call opens its own. Its first recorded reply writes a point span `planner.reply` with after_decision_ms since the decision returned. Injected clock, no content; the parts add up to total_ms.
- **ORCH-526** (agent): The shared `_run_once` (every runtime and role) times prepare (the request built), start, stream (model calls and tools) and close, with model_calls and the runtime's start_steps_ms (RUN-420): the planner's model.turn output `timing` holds them as `call` beside ferb_before, model_call and ferb_after; a worker or checker span carries them as `timing`. A usage report with no timing of the runtime's own gets FERB's from the events' arrival (`by` arrival). Each set adds up to its total_ms.
- **ORCH-527** (agent): ferb/trace/timing.py builds from the recorded timing only, per planner turn: FERB before the model, the runtime's start, each model call split (with whose clock), the lookups' tool calls in the order they began, the stream's remainder, the close and FERB after; per worker or checker run the same without the planner's parts. `--json` adds it as `timing`, `--full` ends with it; a span from before timing shows none. Developer toolbox only (DMN-3); no RPC changes.
- **ORCH-528** (owner): A planner turn has no overall time limit. It is stopped only when its runtime has produced no event (a streamed answer, reasoning or commentary delta, a tool call or its result, a usage report) for the 180 s silence window the other non-worker calls already have, and then FERB replies plainly that it stopped because nothing came back for 3 minutes; it is not tried again behind the owner's back. The 180 s silence guard stays for the other non-worker calls; workers keep no time limit.
- **ORCH-529** (owner): Only messages sent before FERB's first reply to the previous one restart the turn: FERB restarts once and reads them together (related: folded in; unrelated: both answered). Later messages wait their turn, and messages that queued are read together in the next turn. Once FERB has replied, a running task is unaffected. Code enforces at most one restart per turn; the turn has no overall time limit, and each of its planner calls, the restart's included, is stopped only by the silence guard (ORCH-528).
- **ORCH-530** (agent): When the owner stops a task, the answer adds "What I'd found before stopping (not checked):" only with the latest worker report's non-empty answer; a report's reason or summary is never shown there, and with no answer the line is left out.
- **ORCH-531** (agent): The plan runner (waiting on its dependencies or a wait's time/event, starting, done, failed, not_finished, wont_run), the attempt loop (running, checking, retrying) and the shared wait for the owner (needs_you) report only through Supervisor._step_state: one `step` event on the tree's stream and the bus (`task.step`, telemetry) with task, request, step and its task id, part when it answers one, status, waits_on, attempt, started_at, ended_at and a strictly increasing seq; the same state twice sends nothing. Loop rounds and conversation turns report through loop.status.
- **ORCH-532** (agent): A row whose step can never run (a dependency ended unfinished) is settled at once as couldn't-do, not at the plan's end. The card payload (plan event, chat.status, task.resumed_event, outcome) carries `steps`: each step's live state, else what plan_steps recorded. States and times live in memory only (no migration): after a restart a step derives its state from plan_steps and one that runs again starts afresh. A worker's live progress line carries its step's task id (`step_task_id`).
- **ORCH-535** (owner): No separate short version: a direct reply streams its full text and a one-part task's answer is the full answer with FERB's side lines. A multi-part task's saved answer is an index built by code: per part its label and its row's first line (else not finished), the results' paths, N of M done and code's lines; the full rows stay in the card and chat.part, and the planner reads the index whole. "Sites contacted" is a count, the sites are link cards. The chat collapses only an answer taller than the chat area (APP-725).
- **ORCH-536** (owner): FERB's own option questions about whether a task goes on (the attempt-5 check-in, the paused task's "Resume?", a closed tab's "continue?", a runtime offer) take only one of their options: no box on the card, typed words refused ("Pick ..."); in chat the exact-option rule stays. A question from the task (a worker's owner.ask, a plan's ask step, a loop round's question) shows its buttons and a box, always, in a row too; typed words go to the worker as the owner's. Text-only questions are unchanged.
- **ORCH-537** (agent): Question kinds come from structure (capability, approval kind, the asker's tag, options_only). In chat, FERB's checks and check-ins count only as one of their options: the owner's words exactly, else the planner's reading exactly, else FERB asks which. A task's question with options takes the owner's exact words as an option and any other words as their answer; FERB asks which, once, only when the words could also answer another open question. The owner's words stay the recorded answer.
- **ORCH-538** (agent): Any correction steered into a task (chat or a safety check's box) sets aside every open safety check of that task (confirmation, P19 retry, conversation scope; by its request or tree), named or not: superseded, never a No; the action, or a plan's ask step, asks again. Other questions change only when named. The set-aside runs in the same steering apply after the words reached each live worker run; the gateway opens no new question for a run that lacks the task's latest correction.
- **ORCH-539** (agent): Each open question in the planner's open-questions block carries the short label of the running task it belongs to (its asking task's tree; none for a question outside any task), so routing an answer or a correction is less of a guess.
- **ORCH-542** (owner): The planner writes a short name (2-5 words of what it is) for every task, schedule, reminder and timer it creates; plan steps get none. Every heading shows it: reminder cards and their arrival, banners, task cards, the Tasks page, Settings → Schedules & Reminders. The full instruction shows only where the owner opens that item in the app window. A row without a name shows its instruction's first clause cut at ~40 characters (code, no model, no renaming). A reminder phrased short keeps the owner's words; a change keeps a schedule's name unless it writes one. A timer's card says it is a timer.
- **ORCH-543** (agent): Implements APP-300 for the count: a card's done/total (Card.tally: plan event, part events, chat.status, the footer, the saved index) is over the rows it shows: every part of this run, a direct part included (a done row with its answer, drawn like any done row), a part this run changed; never a part an earlier turn finished (a continued run leaves those out of rows and count; whether every ask is done reads the same). A feeder step answers no part: no row, no count. Loop, conversation, stopped and won't-run rows count.
- **ORCH-545** (owner): Supersedes the answer-wording parts of ORCH-309, PRM-323, PRM-326, PRM-327, ORCH-540 and ORCH-541. The checker judges the outcome conditions as before and no longer judges the answer's wording. It returns only findings: a quoted sentence the evidence contradicts or a guess stated as fact, with the evidence. The worker gets one turn to fix those sentences, then a short re-check; if that fails, code removes or marks exactly the quoted sentences. One round, unattended runs too.
- **ORCH-546** (agent): Implements ORCH-545. No runtime resumes an ended worker run, so the fix turn is a new observe-only run of the same worker type and runtime, given its answer and the findings (roles/fix.md, FIX_SCHEMA). recheck.md re-checks only the revised answer. Fallback: contradicted is removed, unsupported is marked; quotes are matched, never meaning. A plan row keeps a fix in progress; after a restart code settles it. Loop and conversation end checks use the same round; an old fix_answer reads as findings.
- **ORCH-547** (agent): Refines ORCH-546. A fallback removal never leaves an answer or row without a letter or digit: it marks the contradicted sentences "(I couldn't confirm this)" instead (answer_marks.settle), and that task, step or part is then never verified: done_unverified with code's standard "Couldn't confirm" line. The fix turn may change only the quoted sentences: outside them the revision must equal the original exactly, and a quote's place may hold no more sentences or lines than the quote (only_quoted_changed); otherwise it is discarded (task.answer_fix_discarded) and the fallback settles the original.
- **ORCH-548** (agent): Refines ORCH-546. The fix turn (<id>.fix) and the re-check (<id>.recheck) release what they hold (tabs, listening) like the worker and its checker: at the attempt's end, a loop round's end and the task's end, when they ran. Their rows end done when they finished (failed or cancelled otherwise), so the tree-end sweep leaves them alone. A plan row keeping a fix in progress also keeps the step's evidence, input notes, conversation proposals, part updates and how note, so after a restart the steps after it read them as before. Findings are taken with every accepting next.
- **ORCH-549** (agent): Refines APP-755's exact-match removal. The planner's copy of a part answered at once is taken out of the plan line only where a whole line or paragraph is exactly that answer (whitespace around it ignored), in the daemon (supervisor.without_whole) and in the app for live and restored turns (ConversationTurn.withoutWhole); never as text inside other words, so a short answer like "4" or "Yes" never cuts a word out of the plan line.
- **ORCH-550** (owner): One schedule may run at several clock times a day and at N random times a day in a window (fresh each day, its next run always known), with an interval too. A schedule's instructions and timing can be changed in place (same id and history; the card shows old and new). One message can make several schedules. Code checks a schedule's words against its saved timing and writes every timing line from it. Each planner turn gets FERB's list of the schedules from its records, and FERB shows that list as a card.
- **ORCH-551** (agent): For ORCH-550. Every clock time written in a new or edited schedule's request (5:20 AM, 6 am, 7.10pm, 18:00; HH:MM 1-11 may be a.m. or p.m.) must be a minute its saved timing runs at: its rule's own times (each run of "every N minutes" over a week), its fixed times, a random window's start or end, or its end's time. Otherwise it goes back to the planner once (with the side entries' quote problems); still mismatched, it is kept and code's line says when it runs and which of those times aren't run times (ORCH-555). Shape only, never what a time is about.
- **ORCH-552** (agent): For ORCH-550. The planner's schedule has times (HH:MM) and random [{count, start, end}]; they follow the rule's days. Random minutes come from the schedule's stored seed and the date, never another run's minute. The timing is kept under `timing` in the schedule's recorded JSON (intent_json), never in rule_json, so an older FERB reads the rule alone and starts. schedule_changes `edit` sets request and/or timing (repeat "" keeps it; times[0] starts an interval) on an active or paused schedule, keeping its id, runs, end, watch and recorded scope; journaled schedule.edited.
- **ORCH-553** (agent): For ORCH-550. A task's part with direct "" (answered by this turn's memory, reminder or schedule entry) must share some of the owner's words with the quote of a remember, forget, timers, schedules, schedule_changes or reminder_cancels entry of the same turn (their places in the owner's message overlap). Otherwise the plan goes back for repair: scheduling happens only in those entries, and a worker has no schedule tool.
- **ORCH-554** (agent): For ORCH-550. Every planner turn's live facts start with the owner's schedules from the database: a count by state, then per schedule its id, name, state, the timing code renders from its rule, its end and watch, its next run and its instructions, marked as the only source for anything about schedules. The planner's show_schedules (a plain boolean) makes code add a schedules card and its line, built from the same rows after the turn's own schedule changes.
- **ORCH-555** (owner): Refines ORCH-551. After the planner's one repair, a new or edited schedule whose instructions still name a clock time it never runs at is saved, not refused; code's line says when it runs and that those times in its instructions are not times it runs.
- **ORCH-556** (owner): Refines ORCH-550. A schedule's random times are drawn in their window with no minimum gap from its other runs (only never the same minute, as built). FERB says what it set (its timing, first and next run); the owner changes it by asking. Nothing more is added.
- **ORCH-557** (agent): Refines ORCH-516. A lookup repeating an earlier call's tool and arguments in the same planner call gets that call's result back, marked as the same and told looking again won't change it; it isn't run again but still counts. A planner call that used all PLANNER_LOOKUPS and then failed gets one last call with no tools, given what its lookups found. Every planner turn's live facts start with the AI FERB uses now, per role, from its settings (connection and model), to answer from.
- **ORCH-558** (agent): Refines ORCH-557 and ORCH-516, for RUN-445 and RUN-446. A planner call that ended without an answer (EmptyAnswer) or was stopped at the wrong-call cap (ToolLoop) gets ORCH-557's one last call: no tools, what its lookups found or that nothing was looked up (PRM-335). The last call's own failure is the turn's, said plainly. A lookup refused because PLANNER_LOOKUPS were spent counts toward the cap. model.turn records last_call (spent, empty, tool_loop). Other failures go on as before.
- **ORCH-559** (owner): Confirms ORCH-516's PLANNER_LOOKUPS = 10 as the owner's limit. When a planner call has made its ten lookups, an eleventh is refused with the gateway's LOOKUPS_SPENT words (answer from what it has, or make the request a task whose worker can look further); a call that then fails gets ORCH-557's one last call, given what its lookups found. The planner chooses an answer or a task; the turn never ends with nothing.
- **ORCH-561** (owner): New literal check kinds a planner condition may name: sent {expected: recipient, site?}, paid {site?}, submitted {site}, trashed / deleted / downloaded {path}. Each is met only when a call of that kind ran without an error with that target in the task's records (a download: a taken browser download); a false one is false whatever the checker said. A task's end adds submit, trash, delete and download cards from the same calls; a file card only for a path that exists.
- **ORCH-562** (owner): Refines ORCH-545. When the worker reported not done, the checker's findings on its answer go to the same one fix turn and re-check as a done answer's, and code removes or marks the quoted sentences of its reason; the checker's own fail reason stays its own. The checker's report includes the availability facts the planner gets (what FERB can use now), so a claim that FERB can't do something can be contradicted.
- **ORCH-563** (owner): Refines ORCH-554. The planner's show (a list of schedules, reminders, tasks, memory, permissions, logins, about; replaces show_schedules, which an older answer still maps to schedules) makes code add each kind's card and line, once, from FERB's rows after the turn's own changes. Every planner turn's live facts list the pending reminders and timers as the schedules are listed: a count by kind, one line each, marked as the truth. The tasks card holds every running task and this chat's ended tasks, each as ORCH-564's task card.
- **ORCH-564** (owner): The planner's about_tasks (a plain list of task ids, ORCH-330) names the tasks a reply states what they did. An id that isn't a running task or one of this chat's is told back once with the side entries' problems; after that it shows nothing. Code adds a task card per id: name, status as code set it, verified, code's couldn't-confirm note, the questions the owner answered for it and its record cards (sends, payments, submits, trash, deletes, downloads, files, sites), with its one line; the record cards are also drawn on their own.
- **ORCH-565** (owner): Refines ORCH-516: about.read joins PLANNER_TOOLS. The self-description gains permissions_in_force (the standing send scopes in force with who holds them, the known destinations and whether each was approved, a digest-kept one named as such, and the end of the owner's ask-free window) and saved_logins (the owner's saved entries by place and name, FERB's own secrets by name, account hint and sites; never a value or a username). The permissions, logins and about cards draw from the same builders.
- **ORCH-566** (owner): A reply's code lines are also recorded apart (chat.reply lines). The planner's history shows a reply code alone wrote as "FERB (code record)"; any other reply as "FERB (reply, model-written, unchecked)" with its prose, then code's lines as "FERB (code record): ...". summary.md never carries current state, and supervisor.md says FERB's earlier replies and the summary are never a source for FERB's state or for what a task did (PRM-340).
- **ORCH-567** (owner): A pause reply starts with code's PAUSED_SAID, the planner's words after it. The profile line in the live facts names the FERB extension's version (its live hello, else the pairing record). Each running task in the status facts names the worker type its runs use (default, or the runtime the owner switched it to). memory.read forgotten lists each forget on record (when, how many items), never contents. A task card lists the questions it asked and the owner's answers, from its owner.ask records.
- **ORCH-568** (agent): Supersedes ORCH-560, for PRM-344. When the worker's last report was not done with a reason and code didn't stop the task, the failed answer is "I couldn't finish this task." with that reason (after ORCH-562's round), then its answer, if any, as "What I found (not checked):"; the checker's fail reason stays the summary and stop_reason. After code's own stop line (_Tree.stop_by_code) only the answer follows that way, unless it is that line. Chosen by where each text came from, never by what it says; an unconfirmed done claim is never shown.
